database.service: disposable PostgreSQL service on 127.0.0.1, one fresh database per process
database.note: Database server CPU and memory are outside this process and are not reported.

method.summary: One Node process hosts the API (Express), the worker entry (processNext), the fixture target, the Judge stand-in and the PostgreSQL client. Runs are launched through POST /api/runs (with model preflight) and executed by the real worker pipeline: session handshake, chat turn, deterministic checks, Judge call, policy gate, persistence.
method.caseMix: 8 prompt-injection cases (expected safe) and 2 unintended-tool-action cases (expected inconclusive: a chat reply cannot prove the absence of writes)

injectedLatency.note: Arbitrary illustrative values, not measurements of any real target or model.

method.cpuAndMemory: Process CPU time and sampled RSS of the whole in-process stack during each phase.

overheadOnly.description: No injected latency: auditor overhead only.

syntheticLatency.description: Target requests +50 ms and Judge calls +100 ms (illustrative).

knownLimits: Fixture only: a local HTTP stand-in replaces the Co-Pilot target and a scripted stand-in replaces the Judge model. No live target, paid provider or model inference was called.

Latencies exclude real target turn time (the documented envelope is up to 90 s per turn) and real model latency, so throughput here is an upper bound on orchestration speed and says nothing about live throughput.
API, worker, fixture and database client share one Node process and one event loop; real deployments separate them. CPU and memory include all of them; PostgreSQL server resources are not included.
The parallel phase serves several targets because a target admits one in-flight run (reservation model); it does not measure contention on a single target.
Adaptive exploration, report drafting, schedules and paid-spend accounting are not part of this throughput run (they are covered functionally by the acceptance tests).
Numbers come from one run on one machine and are not statistically characterized; treat them as a regression baseline for comparing later runs on the same machine, not as an SLO.
This is not the 100-case fixture baseline and scale-cost analysis owned by HDX-32 (P01), and it is not the explicitly authorized live 100-case acceptance owned by HDX-37 (L02).
